answers.ask: Should the eight zones be one continuous world, or separate maps stitched by loading transitions?
answers.answer: Use one continuous open world with natural transitions between all eight zones, as specified in the world layout.

answers.ask: Are the caves and the fortress instanced per party, or shared open world?
answers.answer: Make Spider Demon Caves and the Endgame Demon Fortress instanced per party so their boss encounters, scaling, and raid progression work cleanly.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D open-world action RPG map in a Taishō-era fantasy setting, built as one continuous world with natural transitions across eight zones. Begin in a rural earth-biome Starting Village: a daytime-safe hub with family homes, a small tutorial obstacle course, and paths leading into surrounding woods. A foggy, moonlit Cursed Forest encircles the village and connects to the Butterfly Mansion training grounds, a forge village, and a snowy mountain pass with alpine trails, boulder parkour, and a hidden trainer cave. A woodland route becomes a dark Haunted Road, continuing toward the forge village and its blacksmith area. The forge village and mountain pass each lead to the Spider Demon Caves, a twisting tunnel dungeon instanced per party for boss encounters. Beyond the caves, high icy mountains rise to an Endgame Demon Fortress, also instanced per party, with raid chambers for final bosses. Include a return route from the fortress back toward the starting village. Use day-to-night lighting, rain, fog, and moonlight to reshape visibility across roads, forests, and settlements.
agent_notes: Self-declared open-world action RPG and every system under it is RPG - levels, skill points, a branching tree, quest boards, a boss ladder - so RPG leads alone; the skill's own worked example takes 'Open-world Action RPG' to RPG rather than splitting Action out, and the Action RPG preset already carries the combat framing. Shape is world-hub-dungeon because the two answers together describe exactly that: eight zones as one continuous overworld with the Starting Village named as the hub, and the Spider Caves and Endgame Fortress instanced per party, so the P4 is stated rather than estimated and stands, with P3 on the overworld-to-instance transition and the shops, forge and Butterfly Mansion you go inside. Added gate-progression for the stated zone unlocks and level-and-yen breathing gates, collectible-nodes for the ore and demon-horn gathering behind the forge's crafting, npc-population for the townsfolk who work by day and hide at night, and terrain-relief for the alpine pass and summit, whose tiered cost is the only elevation claim I make. I judged the mountain trainer cave and the twisting Spider tunnels not to earn a P2, since one is a single interior off a hillside and the other is inside an instanced map rather than layered over the overworld, and the tutorial obby is a teaching space rather than a second genre.
